p17/esc215:10.speaker: seeker
p17/esc215:10.text: Are you still with that job now, enough to consider it a career?

p17/esc215:11.speaker: supporter
p17/esc215:11.text: I would say so I am an insurance broker, it has only been a year or so but there seems to be room to move up. You can find something too

p17/esc215:12.speaker: seeker
p17/esc215:12.text: Is there any advice for getting out of my situation?

p17/esc215:14.speaker: supporter
p17/esc215:14.text: Can you give me some more details?

p17/esc215:15.speaker: seeker
p17/esc215:15.text: I just find the work mundane and way too remedial

p17/esc215:17.speaker: seeker
p17/esc215:17.text: did you look at any websites or other job searching tools before you found your new job?

p17/esc215:18.speaker: supporter
p17/esc215:18.text: I have you a few, there are also many ways to gain skills online that buff up your resume a bit

p17/esc215:19.speaker: seeker
p17/esc215:19.text: what types of skill can I gain online?

p17/esc215:20.speaker: supporter
p17/esc215:20.text: Indeed is one of the better ones to look for jobs, honestly I would suggest looking at jobs that you normally wouldn't and see what kind of qualifications they need and see if you can get that done online.

p17/esc215:21.speaker: seeker
p17/esc215:21.text: so filter based on my absolute needs and go for online skills that I can complete?

p17/esc215:22.speaker: supporter
p17/esc215:22.text: yes I think that is a great idea, look for jobs that meet your needs and figure out what you can do to look attractive to employers

p17/esc215:23.speaker: seeker
p17/esc215:23.text: I have tried glassdoor before, have you had any luck there?

p17/esc215:24.speaker: supporter
p17/esc215:24.text: I used it a bit, I mainly used indeed.

p17/esc215:25.speaker: seeker
p17/esc215:25.text: and have you showcased your skills using LinkedIn before? I have had that one recommended to me before, they said its a great way to neatly organize accomplishments and personal background

p17/esc215:26.speaker: supporter
p17/esc215:26.text: Yes especially if you are applying for anything in a professional setting that is very important.

p17/esc215:27.speaker: seeker
p17/esc215:27.text: do you have any examples of online skills you completed?

p17/esc215:28.speaker: supporter
p17/esc215:28.text: coursera has a lot of great courses, it really depends on what you are looking for.

p17/esc215:29.speaker: seeker
p17/esc215:29.text: if I was looking to enter the engineering field, any recommendations?

p17/esc215:30.speaker: supporter
p17/esc215:30.text: Is that what you are going to school for?

p17/esc215:31.speaker: seeker
p17/esc215:31.text: yes but I may change my mind

p17/esc215:32.speaker: supporter
p17/esc215:32.text: What year are you in? most engineering programs have a practicum and that is a great opportunity to make contacts and potentially get offered a job

p17/esc215:33.speaker: seeker
p17/esc215:33.text: yes I have been networking as I go

p17/esc215:34.speaker: supporter
p17/esc215:34.text: Honestly you seem like you are pretty on top of this I don't think you will have any issues finding a job.

p17/esc215:35.speaker: seeker
p17/esc215:35.text: yeah I mean the topic was about final exam stress but we got on a tangent

p17/esc215:36.speaker: supporter
p17/esc215:36.text: Yes that is fair enough, how much time do you have until your exam?

p17/esc215:38.speaker: supporter
p17/esc215:38.text: While that is plenty of time to get some studying done:)

p17/esc215:39.speaker: seeker
p17/esc215:39.text: yes I probably should, thank you for your insight!

p17/esc215:4.speaker: seeker
p17/esc215:4.text: I need ways alleviate stress while studying

p17/esc215:40.speaker: supporter
p17/esc215:40.text: Honestly I find that if you are going for the test right away I always like to just breath and relax a bit.

p17/esc215:41.speaker: seeker
p17/esc215:41.text: yeah no use in cramming for more info when I could just chill out

p17/esc215:42.speaker: supporter
p17/esc215:42.text: You seem like you know what you are doing, I think you will do just fine

p17/esc215:5.speaker: supporter
p17/esc215:5.text: It sounds like you are having some difficulty at school, I have definitely been there.

p17/esc215:6.speaker: seeker
p17/esc215:6.text: yeah, it can be tough sometimes and feel like you're in a dead end situation

p17/esc215:7.speaker: supporter
p17/esc215:7.text: Yes I worked a dead end job for ages when I was younger and sometimes you just feel stuck

p17/esc215:8.speaker: seeker
p17/esc215:8.text: How did you push past that job?

p17/esc215:9.speaker: supporter
p17/esc215:9.text: I am going to be honest a little luck was involved I managed to impress a customer that came in and ended up applying at their work.

p17/esc629:0.speaker: supporter
p17/esc629:0.text: How can I help you today?

p17/esc629:1.speaker: seeker
p17/esc629:1.text: I'm disgusted with my professors that they don't see me as a human with real emotions and feelings.

p17/esc629:10.speaker: seeker
p17/esc629:10.text: That sounds like a good idea.  Maybe they are feeling this way too.

p17/esc629:11.speaker: supporter
p17/esc629:11.text: Also sometimes just stepping back and taking some deep breaths can help to alleviate some anxieties. Have you tried that ever?

p17/esc629:12.speaker: seeker
p17/esc629:12.text: I will have to give that a try.  I've done that in the past and had forgotten just how much that helped me before.

p17/esc629:13.speaker: supporter
p17/esc629:13.text: That is reassuring that it worked before for you and  can work again.

p17/esc629:14.speaker: seeker
p17/esc629:14.text: I'm so worried about failing because I just don't feel the support from my professors to care either way for my successes.  It's so different from high school and home when my parents encouraged me and supported me full-heartedly.

p17/esc629:15.speaker: supporter
p17/esc629:15.text: College can be quite a change from the protective atmosphere of home.  Have you tried any support groups or religious groups for encouragement?

p17/esc629:16.speaker: seeker
p17/esc629:16.text: I am religious so perhaps I could seek a group out and they could help with encouraging me.

p17/esc629:17.speaker: supporter
p17/esc629:17.text: I was a  part of a religious group in college and they were very supportive even praying for me on exam days.  I felt they helped me with my success by planting seeds of positive feedback to me.

p17/esc629:18.speaker: seeker
p17/esc629:18.text: I used to be part of one during high school years, and that sounds like it would help.

p17/esc629:19.speaker: supporter
p17/esc629:19.text: Are you starting to feel better about the situation?

p17/esc629:2.speaker: supporter
p17/esc629:2.text: I understand that you are feeling like your professors don't see you as a person with feelings. What happened to make you feel this way?

p17/esc629:20.speaker: seeker
p17/esc629:20.text: Yes, I do thinking about other people filling in the gaps and supporting me when others won't or can't. Thanks for chatting.  This was helpful.

p17/esc629:21.speaker: supporter
p17/esc629:21.text: You are welcome.  I wish you well.

p17/esc629:22.speaker: seeker
p17/esc629:22.text: I think I have a few tools now to make things better.

p17/esc629:3.speaker: seeker
p17/esc629:3.text: I have testing all the time and study non-stop, but the professors don't seem to encourage or support me.  They just see me as a number I feel.

p17/esc629:4.speaker: supporter
p17/esc629:4.text: That's hard to feel like they are treating you like a number when you are working so hard.  Have you talked to them about it?

p17/esc629:5.speaker: seeker
p17/esc629:5.text: It's hard to trust them when I'm seen as 1 of 100 people.  If I am struggling they don't flinch or ask me how they can assist.  I just am expected to

p17/esc629:7.speaker: supporter
p17/esc629:7.text: I had a similar experience in my college days. It was very difficult to have so much pressure to succeed and feel so alone.  You can do though because you are working hard and want to succeed.

p17/esc629:8.speaker: seeker
p17/esc629:8.text: Thanks for the encouragement.  Where do I start to help myself feel better?

p17/esc629:9.speaker: supporter
p17/esc629:9.text: I see you are anxious about this when talking to you, but have you thought about getting some support from other students in your position?

p17/esc67:1.speaker: seeker
p17/esc67:1.text: I am really very angry with my friends for not inviting me

p17/esc67:10.speaker: seeker
p17/esc67:10.text: In last 2 events only , what about you

p17/esc67:12.speaker: supporter
p17/esc67:12.text: I know it is hard at times, but be strong.

p17/esc67:14.speaker: seeker
p17/esc67:14.text: sometime it will happen , but we should forget and move on

p17/esc67:15.speaker: seeker
p17/esc67:15.text: How many best friends do you have ?

p17/esc67:3.speaker: seeker
p17/esc67:3.text: I didn't did any anything wrong to my friends but they are simply saying they forget me

p17/esc67:4.speaker: seeker
p17/esc67:4.text: So they no need on me ,

p17/esc67:5.speaker: seeker
p17/esc67:5.text: I am not important person to them

p17/esc67:6.speaker: supporter
p17/esc67:6.text: I have been angry with friends as well, but time loves a hero, as they say.

p17/esc67:7.speaker: seeker
p17/esc67:7.text: In my all events i am inviting them all but how they

p17/esc67:9.speaker: supporter
p17/esc67:9.text: How long have your friends been neglecting you??

p17/esc85:0.speaker: supporter
p17/esc85:0.text: Hello there! How can I encourage you today?

p17/esc85:1.speaker: seeker
p17/esc85:1.text: Hi, I have been going through a lot of stress with school and am also sad and lonely as of late and not sure how to make myself feel better

p17/esc85:10.speaker: supporter
p17/esc85:10.text: I remember after each class, I would take 15 minutes to review all my notes from class, that seems short, but really, it adds up and helped so much.

p17/esc85:11.speaker: seeker
p17/esc85:11.text: Yes, I think you have excellent advice about organization. I feel like I lose track of what I have and when to do it. I also bounce between classes, feeling stressed because there is so much. Do you think doing one class at a time is best?

p17/esc85:12.speaker: seeker
p17/esc85:12.text: I also tend to save stuff sometimes so I have a lot of work build up with tests on the same days. I am not sure how to stop procrastinating.

p17/esc85:13.speaker: supporter
p17/esc85:13.text: Yes, stick to one subject at a time. For example, if you think 1/2 hour is good enough to study, then stick to that. When done, your done until the next time it is on your schedule.

p17/esc85:14.speaker: seeker
p17/esc85:14.text: Ok. Thank you so much for the ideas. It seems like you have had similar experiences with stress from school.

p17/esc85:15.speaker: supporter
p17/esc85:15.text: Procrastination never makes us feel good. If I keep putting something off, I then feel guilty. If I make a goal, and I reach it, I can put a reward. For example, if you study 3 subjects 1/2 hour each, you can go out for yogurt with a friend. So you reward yourself for sticking to that goal.

p17/esc85:16.speaker: supporter
p17/esc85:16.text: Yes, I did. lol I'm really old now. This technique I use in all my life. Even house chores, I break it down into a schedule, put it in writing, then check off what I do. Then I feel good about my accomplishments.

p17/esc85:17.speaker: seeker
p17/esc85:17.text: Yes, that was my other question to you. It sounds great to just do a little time for each class but I often get overwhelmed and need a break

p17/esc85:18.speaker: seeker
p17/esc85:18.text: I have never used check lists or planners. I think it is part of how I get overwhelmed maybe.

p17/esc85:19.speaker: supporter
p17/esc85:19.text: Definitely you need a break, so schedule them as rewards. You can even do 15 minutes in say 4 subjects, then take a walk, take a cup of tea, or call a friend, then back to the books.

p17/esc85:2.speaker: supporter
p17/esc85:2.text: So you have had a lot of stress with school lately and are struggling to keep yourself cheerful?

p17/esc85:20.speaker: supporter
p17/esc85:20.text: Keep it as SIMPLE as possible, don't get bogged down. I used to think planning was TERRIBLE< but actually, it sets one FREE. You feel so much better and accomplished when you see how much you have done. It really is amazing.

p17/esc85:21.speaker: supporter
p17/esc85:21.text: HOw man classes do you have?

p17/esc85:24.speaker: supporter
p17/esc85:24.text: That's a lot but it is totally doable. Here is a good example, If you plant seeds in a garden today, you have to weed it a bit tomorrow, the next day, the next day, you have to wait for rain, then weed some more, the harvest comes and YAY! You are happy. But if you lie on your bed, never planting, never weeding, you procrastinate, you get nothing.

p17/esc85:25.speaker: supporter
p17/esc85:25.text: If you write your classes down and then write a reasonable time to study each one. Maybe 3 today, 3 tomorrow, then add rewards if you do that, maybe make a list of rewards, so you can pick and choose, then you check off when you do the subject.  Like a chore chart.

p17/esc85:26.speaker: seeker
p17/esc85:26.text: Yes haha. That is a good comparison. You have been super helpful. I will for sure try to use your advice. Thank you!

p17/esc85:27.speaker: seeker
p17/esc85:27.text: Have a great day and thanks again

p17/esc85:28.speaker: supporter
p17/esc85:28.text: You are quite welcome! God bless have a great day!

p17/esc85:3.speaker: supporter
p17/esc85:3.text: Is there something in particular at school that is stressing you out? Exams? Relationships?

p17/esc85:4.speaker: seeker
p17/esc85:4.text: Yes! Its very hard to keep positive with all the work I have and I feel I am not doing well.

p17/esc85:5.speaker: seeker
p17/esc85:5.text: Yes, I have a lot of exams right now and that on top of not hanging out with friends a lot lately has made life tough.

p17/esc85:6.speaker: supporter
p17/esc85:6.text: I can understand being stressed if you think you are not doing well in school and have a lot of work. How are your grades now?

p17/esc85:7.speaker: seeker
p17/esc85:7.text: I still have decent grades but I feel like I am not prepared for big exams currently and they are worth a lot

p17/esc85:8.speaker: supporter
p17/esc85:8.text: Yes, that can be tough. When I had a lot of tests coming up and a lot to study for, I wrote down goals to study -- like I broke down the classes and made certain goals to study a bit in each class. And then if I did that, I could go out with friends or some reward like that.

p17/esc85:9.speaker: supporter
p17/esc85:9.text: For example, if you have 7 classes, you can make a chart for when you will study for each of those classes and then check them off as you accomplish it, maybe not all in one day, maybe break it up in reasonable bits. Then study according to your goal, if that makes sense.

p17/p17_conv_6:0.speaker: supporter
p17/p17_conv_6:0.text: Hey Andrew, how have you been feeling lately?

p17/p17_conv_6:1.speaker: seeker
p17/p17_conv_6:1.text: Hey, honestly, I've been a bit overwhelmed. I'm considering changing my research focus, and it's been weighing on me.

p17/p17_conv_6:2.speaker: supporter
p17/p17_conv_6:2.text: I can imagine that must be a tough decision. What’s making you think about changing your focus?

p17/p17_conv_6:3.speaker: seeker
p17/p17_conv_6:3.text: I haven't made much progress lately, and I'm just not interested in my current topic anymore. Plus, the feedback from my advisor was disheartening.

p17/p17_conv_6:4.speaker: supporter
p17/p17_conv_6:4.text: That sounds really frustrating. Feedback like that can really bring you down, especially when you're already feeling uncertain. How did you feel after hearing it?

p17/p17_conv_6:5.speaker: seeker
p17/p17_conv_6:5.text: I felt a bit lost, to be honest. Like I’m just not cut out for this. It's hard because it makes me question my decisions.

p17/p17_conv_6:6.speaker: supporter
p17/p17_conv_6:6.text: It's completely normal to question yourself when you're going through such challenges. Remember, you’ve made it this far for a reason. What do you think would rekindle your interest in research?

p17/p17_conv_6:7.speaker: seeker
p17/p17_conv_6:7.text: I've been considering exploring alternative energy sources, like renewables. It's something that aligns with my values and seems rewarding.

330ee5b41e6f2d2195763230969d215369cb6102.head: ME
330ee5b41e6f2d2195763230969d215369cb6102.statement: seeker reflects on feeling stuck in a mundane academic situation and compares it to being in a dead-end job

spans.speaker: seeker
spans.exact_quote: yeah, it can be tough sometimes and feel like you're in a dead end situation

8e0a36decd85c4fbb459eb75e3d6f7ef68fd4a25.head: ME
8e0a36decd85c4fbb459eb75e3d6f7ef68fd4a25.statement: needing breaks due to overwhelm while studying

spans.speaker: seeker
spans.exact_quote: Yes, that was my other question to you. It sounds great to just do a little time for each class but I often get overwhelmed and need a break
